title: Bethlehem's hidden mysteries versus Zion's open fulfillment
english: You leavened the bread, but Zion displayed a supper. You nourished the calf at the manger, but Zion led it up to the altar. You hid Jesus in swaddling clothes, but she bared his side to Thomas when he wished to touch it. You have a virgin giving birth while the organs of nature remained closed; she has a bridal chamber that, while the doors were closed, receives the bridegroom within and holds him.
translator_notes: The Greek text begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence.
The final clause is an edge fragment.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum Lazarum (Khazarzar) u01 rem early
orientation: Hesychius continues his comparison between Bethlehem, where Christ's mysteries were hidden, and Zion, where they are now revealed and fulfilled.

title: How to praise James, the servant and brother of Christ
english: How shall I praise the servant and brother of Christ, the commander-in-chief of the new Jerusalem, the leader of the priests, the chief of the apostles, the crown among heads, the one shining beyond among lamps, the one shining beyond among stars? Peter speaks in public, but James gives the law, and a few words contracted the magnitude of the question: “I judge not to trouble those from the nations,” and so on (Acts 15:19).
translator_notes: The Greek text begins mid-sentence with δοῦλον καὶ ἀδελφόν and ends mid-sentence with οὗ τὴν κρῑσιν ἀθετεῖν οὐ, indicating a fragmentary passage.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum Lazarum (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid
orientation: Hesychius, the preacher, is asking how he can worthily praise James, the brother of the Lord, after contrasting Bethlehem and Zion.

title: The Judge Speaks Through James
english: “I judge.” It is not lawful to set aside his judgment, nor to despise his decree. For in me speaks the judge of all, both the dead and the living. The instrument is mine, but the craftsman is above me. I supply the tongue, but the Word, the maker, supplies the word. Pay no attention to the reed, but to the one who writes with it. Let obedience follow the hearing.
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence: ...θέμις, οὐδὲ φαυλίζειν τὸ ψήφισμα...
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum Lazarum (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
orientation: Hesychius is explaining that James's words at the apostolic council are not merely human, but the voice of Christ the judge of all speaking through James as an instrument.
